content.text: productive cough for ≥3mo/y for 2+ consecutive years
accompanied by destruction of the airspace walls

: begins w chronic airway inflam that progresses to emphysema, a condition characterized by irreversible bronchial narrowing & alveolar hyperinflation ⇢ loss of diffusion area → V/Q mismatch w/ resultant hypoxemia & hypercapnia
▪︎⇣ DLCO: establishes presence of emphysema (norm in chronic bronchitis)
(ex, enlrg lungs, flattened diaphragm, ⇡ AP diameter)
PaO2 ≤55mmHg = an indication for cont supplemental O2
➁ Assessment of airflow limitation (% of predicted FEV1 ⇢ GOLD)
➂ Sx/exacerbation Hx (mMRC dyspnea scale, CAT score)
▪︎bronchodilator (long-acting preferred over short-acting, except w/ very occasional breathlessness)
*single inhaler tx may be more convenient + effective than multiple inhalers
▪︎Bronchodilators are the backbone. A LAMA or LABA is first-line maintenance, with a SABA (± SAMA) PRN for everyone.
▪︎ICS is add-on only, as triple therapy (LABA + LAMA + ICS) for patients with: eos ≥300, or eos ≥100 plus ≥2 moderate exacerbations or ≥1 hospitalization per year despite LABA + LAMA.
▪︎ICS is unlikely to help when eos <100, and should be avoided with recurrent pneumonia or a history of mycobacterial infection.
▪︎LABA + ICS without a LAMA is no longer encouraged (GOLD 2023+). If ICS is indicated, go straight to triple therapy.
▪︎ICS adverse effects: pneumonia, oral thrush, hoarseness, bruising.
*mortality benefit directly prop to # of hrs used
of resp Sx necessitating additional therapy
: advanced age, productive cough, longer duration of COPD,
(exclude PNA, PTX, pulm edema, pleural effusion)
indicated if chgs in ≥2 cardinal SXS
